objetivo.en: Link, sum up and close an informal story with «pues nada», «total que» and «bueno pues».

traduccion.en: well then, so, anyway

nota.en: Say “pwehs NAH-dah”: the d between vowels is soft, like the th in “this”. It opens a sentence to pick up the thread or to close a topic, with a tone that is resigned or decided, and it is followed by a comma. It is heard in Spain, in Mexico and in much of Latin America.

traduccion.en: so, in the end, the result was

nota.en: Say “toh-TAHL keh”. It introduces the result of a story you have just told: Total que llegamos tarde. It is not the same as en total (in total, all together). It is heard in Spain and also in Mexico and other Latin American countries, mostly when telling a story informally.

traduccion.en: well then, all right then

nota.en: Say “BWEH-noh pwehs”. It marks a change of topic or a soft goodbye, and it is often written «bueno, pues». It works in every Spanish-speaking country.

traduccion.en: anyway, in short

nota.en: Say “ehn FEEN”. It closes a thought, often with a shrug and a little resignation: En fin, ya pasó.

traduccion.en: the relaxed chat among friends

nota.en: Say “tehr-TOO-lyah”: the stress falls on TOO and the li sounds like “ly”. A tertulia is an informal gathering where people talk at length with no hurry.

traduccion.en: the story

nota.en: Say “KWEHN-toh”. In everyday talk, el cuento is the story you tell about what happened to you. It also means a short story or a tale for children.

traduccion.en: the hassle, the long tedious thing

nota.en: Say “RROH-yoh”: the first r is trilled and ll sounds like the y in “yes”. It is informal: ¡Qué rollo! means What a hassle! The word also exists in Spain.

traduccion.en: the sunset, the late afternoon

nota.en: Say “ah-tahr-deh-SEHR”: the stress falls on the last syllable and the c before e sounds like an s. It is the time of day when the sun goes down.

explicacion.en: English “well” as a filler is not bien: bien is the adverb of “good, well” (hablas bien). To say “well then” and say goodbye softly, Spanish uses bueno pues.
English “so” before a result is not así alone: así means “like this” or “that way”, so the sentence says “That is how we arrived late”. To sum up what happened, use total que (or así que).
Learners hear “total” and think of “in total”. For an amount, Spanish says en total. Total que is only the marker that introduces the result of a story.

titulo.en: Little words that organize a story

texto.en: When Spanish speakers tell a story among friends (el cuento), they use small words that carry almost no meaning but organize the story. This lesson has three of them. «Total que» sums up a long story and gives its result: «Esperé una hora el bus, empezó a llover y total que volví caminando». «Pues nada» picks the thread up again or closes a topic with a resigned or decided tone: «Pues nada, lo llamo mañana». «Bueno pues» changes the topic or says goodbye softly: «Bueno pues, nos vemos mañana». «En fin» also closes a thought, usually with a shrug.

They go at the beginning of the clause. «Pues nada» and «bueno pues» are followed by a comma; «total que» is followed directly by the result, in the indicative: «Total que llegamos tarde». Do not translate them word by word: «pues nada» is not “then nothing”, and «total que» has nothing to do with «en total» (all together). They belong to relaxed talk among friends (tertulia). Do not overuse them: one of each in a story is enough. All of these are used in Spain and also in Mexico and other Latin American countries, especially when telling a story informally.

contexto.en: Sunday, January 21, 2035, in the afternoon. Emma and Mateo are at a beach in Atacames, on the last day of their working weekend (Saturday and Sunday). They sit under an umbrella with a juice, using tú, and tell each other how the weekend went. Mateo arrived on Saturday night after a long bus trip; Emma had worked alone in a café. Emma is still at Andes Vivos and prepares Puente in her free time.

dialogo.texto: Mira qué tarde tan linda, Mateo. El jugo está frío, la sombrilla nos da sombra y por fin tenemos una tertulia tranquila.

traduccion.en: Look what a lovely afternoon, Mateo. The juice is cold, the umbrella gives us shade and we finally have a relaxed chat.

dialogo.texto: Sí, lo necesitaba. Todavía estoy cansado del viaje de ayer; dormí poco y mal.

traduccion.en: Yes, I needed it. I'm still tired from yesterday's trip; I slept little and badly.

dialogo.texto: Anoche solo me dijiste que el bus tuvo un problema. Todavía no me contaste bien por qué llegaste de noche.

traduccion.en: Last night you only told me the bus had a problem. You still haven't told me properly why you arrived at night.

dialogo.texto: Es una historia larga, pero te cuento el cuento completo. Salí de Quito el sábado a las siete de la mañana y el bus iba lleno.

traduccion.en: It's a long story, but I'll tell you the whole thing. I left Quito on Saturday at seven in the morning and the bus was full.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y todo iba bien?

traduccion.en: And was everything going well?

dialogo.texto: Hasta la mitad del camino. Ahí el motor empezó a hacer un ruido horrible y el chofer tuvo que parar en plena carretera.

traduccion.en: Until halfway. Then the engine started making a horrible noise and the driver had to stop in the middle of the road.

dialogo.texto: ¿En plena carretera? ¿Sin sombra y sin nada? Pobre de ti.

traduccion.en: In the middle of the road? With no shade and nothing? Poor you.

dialogo.texto: Sin sombra y sin agua. El chofer dijo que otro bus llegaba en media hora. Esperé una hora y nada.

traduccion.en: No shade and no water. The driver said another bus was coming in half an hour. I waited an hour and nothing.

dialogo.texto: ¡Una hora bajo el sol! Qué rollo.

traduccion.en: An hour under the sun! What a hassle.

dialogo.texto: Después empezó a llover. Total que una señora me prestó su paraguas, otro bus por fin paró y llegué a Atacames cuando ya era de noche.

traduccion.en: Then it started to rain. So in the end a lady lent me her umbrella, another bus finally stopped and I got to Atacames when it was already night.

dialogo.texto: O sea que saliste de mañana y llegaste de noche.

traduccion.en: So you left in the morning and arrived at night.

dialogo.texto: Exacto. En fin, ya pasó, y lo importante es que llegué. ¿Y tu sábado, cómo te fue?

traduccion.en: Exactly. Anyway, it's over, and the important thing is that I made it. And how was your Saturday?

dialogo.texto: Más tranquilo que el tuyo. Llegué a las diez, pero el cuarto del hotel todavía no estaba listo. Pues nada, me senté en un café frente al mar a trabajar con la computadora.

traduccion.en: Calmer than yours. I arrived at ten, but the hotel room wasn't ready yet. So, well, I sat in a café facing the sea to work on my computer.

dialogo.texto: Qué buena oficina, con vista al mar.

traduccion.en: What a great office, with a view of the sea.

dialogo.texto: Eso pensé yo. Pero a mediodía se cayó el internet en todo el pueblo. Pues nada, saqué un cuaderno y terminé la lista de clientes a mano.

traduccion.en: That's what I thought. But at noon the internet went down in the whole town. So, well, I took out a notebook and finished the client list by hand.

dialogo.texto: ¿A mano? Eso sí que es amor por el trabajo.

traduccion.en: By hand? That is real love for the job.

dialogo.texto: Total que cuando llegaste tú, ya tenía cuatro páginas escritas y la cena fría.

traduccion.en: So by the time you arrived, I already had four pages written and a cold dinner.

dialogo.texto: Perdón por la cena. Hoy pago yo. Oye, hablando de lo que escribiste, en el bus tuve mucho tiempo para pensar en el nombre de la agencia.

traduccion.en: Sorry about the dinner. Tonight's on me. Listen, speaking of what you wrote, on the bus I had a lot of time to think about the name of the agency.

dialogo.texto: ¿Puente? Pensé que ya lo habíamos decidido.

traduccion.en: Puente? I thought we had already decided.

dialogo.texto: Sí, pero quería estar seguro de que suena bien en español y en inglés.

traduccion.en: Yes, but I wanted to be sure it sounds good in Spanish and in English.

dialogo.texto: Un puente une dos orillas, y eso es lo que queremos: unir a los viajeros con las comunidades. A mí me encanta.

traduccion.en: A bridge joins two shores, and that is what we want: to join travelers with the communities. I love it.

dialogo.texto: A mí también. Total que seguimos con Puente, y el logo ya casi está terminado. Tiene un puente azul y el sol detrás.

traduccion.en: Me too. So we keep Puente, and the logo is almost finished. It has a blue bridge with the sun behind it.

dialogo.texto: Qué lindo. Pues nada, lo vemos mañana en Quito con calma. Ahora no quiero otra tertulia de trabajo.

traduccion.en: How lovely. Well, we'll look at it tomorrow in Quito, calmly. Right now I don't want another work chat.

dialogo.texto: Tienes razón. ¿Qué hora es? Mira cómo se pone el cielo.

traduccion.en: You're right. What time is it? Look how the sky is turning.

dialogo.texto: El atardecer ya empezó. Mira esos colores, no quiero perderlo.

traduccion.en: The sunset has already started. Look at those colors, I don't want to miss it.

dialogo.texto: Yo tampoco. Mañana ya es lunes y volvemos a la rutina.

traduccion.en: Me neither. Tomorrow is already Monday and we go back to the routine.

dialogo.texto: Bueno pues, dejamos los cuentos para después y vamos a ver el atardecer. Luego buscamos algo de cenar.

traduccion.en: Well then, we'll leave the stories for later and go see the sunset. Then we'll look for something to eat.

dialogo.texto: Vamos. Y esta vez, sin buses averiados.

traduccion.en: Let's go. And this time, no broken-down buses.

dialogo.texto: Y sin lluvia, por favor. Solo nosotros, el mar y el jugo.

traduccion.en: And no rain, please. Just us, the sea and the juice.

consigna.en: Why did Mateo arrive at night?

feedback.en: The bus broke down on the road, he waited an hour, it rained, and he took another bus. He did not get lost or oversleep.

traduccion.en: by the way

nota.en: Say “pohr SYEHR-toh”: the c before i sounds like an s. It brings in something you remember in passing because of what was just said. It does not mean “certainly”.

nota.en: Say “ah loh keh EE-bah”: iba is the imperfect of ir. It brings the conversation back to the main topic after a detour. When several people were talking, say a lo que íbamos.

nota.en: Say “ehn-teh-RAHR-seh deh”. It is a reflexive verb and it takes de: ¿Te enteraste de lo del congreso? Do not confuse it with entrar (to go in).

nota.en: Say “een-TEHR-preh-teh”: the written accent marks the stress on TEHR. It is the person who translates speech aloud. The same form is used for men and women: el / la intérprete.

traduccion.en: while at it, in passing

nota.en: Say “deh PAH-soh”. It adds a second action that you do on the same trip or at the same time: Voy al banco y, de paso, compro pan.

traduccion.en: to bring up the subject

nota.en: Say “sah-KAHR ehl TEH-mah”. You use it when someone starts talking about something: Sacó el tema del congreso.

traduccion.en: the writing workshop

nota.en: Say “tah-YEHR deh ehs-kree-TOO-rah”: ll sounds like the y in “yes” and the stress of escritura falls on TOO. A taller is a workshop where people learn by doing.

traduccion.en: the gossip, the piece of gossip

nota.en: Say “CHEES-meh”: ch as in “church”. In Latin America chisme is the usual word for a piece of gossip that is not confirmed.

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Por cierto, ¿te conté que me mudo?

explicacion.en: Learners translate “by the way” word by word. Por el camino means “along the road”. To add something in passing, Spanish says por cierto.
Enterarse looks like English “enter”, but entrar means “to go in”. To find out about something, use enterarse de and the reflexive pronoun (te enteraste).

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Sí, por cierto, voy a la fiesta.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Sí, por supuesto, voy a la fiesta.

explicacion.en: Por cierto looks like “certainly”, but it means “by the way”. For “of course, certainly”, Spanish says por supuesto or claro.

titulo.en: Changing the topic without breaking the chat

texto.en: In a relaxed conversation, topics do not follow a strict order: something someone says reminds you of something else. «Por cierto» is the Spanish way to bring it in: «Por cierto, ¿te conté que me mudo?». It always connects with what was just said (even loosely) and usually gives news: «¿te conté…?», «¿te dije…?», «¿sabías que…?», «¿te enteraste de…?». When the detour is over, you return to the main topic with «bueno, a lo que iba» (one person) or «a lo que íbamos» (several people).

titulo.en: What to do and what not to do

texto.en: After «por cierto» you use a question or a statement in the indicative: «¿te conté que Lucía se casa?». With «¿te enteraste de…?» the verb takes de: «¿te enteraste de lo del congreso?». «De paso» adds a second action in the same breath, and «sacar el tema» means to bring up a subject. Avoid «por cierto» to disagree, to say goodbye or to say “certainly”: it only introduces a related piece of news. These phrases belong to talk among friends; with someone you do not know well you can use them in the same way, but with usted.

contexto.en: Wednesday, January 24, 2035, late afternoon. After a meeting at the institute, Emma, Sofía and Andrés have coffee at a café in La Mariscal. They have been friends for years and use tú with each other. Emma still works at Andes Vivos and prepares Puente in her free time; she wants to go over Puente's agenda and the client list with them.

dialogo.texto: Qué reunión tan larga. Necesitaba este café con urgencia, de verdad.

traduccion.en: What a long meeting. I badly needed this coffee, really.

dialogo.texto: Yo también, y mira que todavía quedan pasteles.

traduccion.en: Me too, and look, there are still some cakes left.

dialogo.texto: Ya que estamos los tres juntos, quiero repasar la agenda de Puente. Primero, la lista de clientes: ya tenemos un grupo de Canadá, seis personas, en preventa, y estoy muy contenta.

traduccion.en: Since the three of us are together, I want to go over Puente's agenda. First, the client list: we already have a group from Canada, six people, in presale, and I'm very happy.

dialogo.texto: Seis personas, ¡qué bien! ¿Y ya tienen hotel?

traduccion.en: Six people, great! And do you have a hotel already?

dialogo.texto: Sí, y un hotel de Baños nos va a regalar el desayuno. Es un buen comienzo, ¿verdad?

traduccion.en: Yes, and a hotel in Baños is going to give us breakfast as a gift. It's a good start, isn't it?

dialogo.texto: Muy buen comienzo. Por cierto, ¿sabes que el instituto busca un intérprete para un congreso? Me enteré esta mañana.

traduccion.en: A very good start. By the way, do you know that the institute is looking for an interpreter for a congress? I found out this morning.

dialogo.texto: ¿Un intérprete? ¿Para qué idiomas?

traduccion.en: An interpreter? For which languages?

dialogo.texto: Del español al inglés, para unos invitados de Estados Unidos. Pensé en Puente, porque ustedes ofrecen interpretación. Serían dos días de conferencias y el instituto quiere a alguien que conozca bien el turismo.

traduccion.en: From Spanish to English, for some guests from the United States. I thought of Puente, because you offer interpreting. It would be two days of lectures and the institute wants someone who knows tourism well.

dialogo.texto: Qué buena idea, Andrés. Me interesa mucho, porque es justo lo que hacemos en Puente. ¿Cuándo es el congreso?

dialogo.texto: Todavía no me dan la fecha, pero te aviso en cuanto la sepa. Seguro que será dentro de unas semanas.

traduccion.en: They haven't given me the date yet, but I'll let you know as soon as I know it. It will surely be in a few weeks.

dialogo.texto: Hablando de novedades, por cierto, ¿les conté que voy a dirigir un taller de escritura en el instituto?

traduccion.en: I didn't know! Congratulations, Sofía. What is the workshop about?

dialogo.texto: Es para escribir artículos y textos largos, en español y en inglés. Empieza pronto, y estás invitada, Emma.

traduccion.en: It's for writing articles and long texts, in Spanish and in English. It starts soon, and you're invited, Emma.

dialogo.texto: Sofía, ¿te enteraste de lo de Pablo, el de la biblioteca? Dicen que se va a vivir a Cuenca.

traduccion.en: Sofía, did you hear about Pablo, the one from the library? They say he's going to live in Cuenca.

dialogo.texto: No sabía nada. Los chismes del instituto siempre te llegan primero a ti.

dialogo.texto: Soy el coordinador, me entero de todo. Pero por ahora es solo un chisme y no hay nada seguro.

traduccion.en: I'm the coordinator, I find out about everything. But for now it's only gossip and nothing is certain.

dialogo.texto: Tranquilo, no digo nada.

traduccion.en: Relax, I won't say a thing.

dialogo.texto: Bueno, a lo que iba: la lista de clientes. Tenemos a los de Canadá y todavía falta confirmar el segundo grupo.

traduccion.en: Well, as I was saying: the client list. We have the people from Canada and we still have to confirm the second group.

dialogo.texto: Por cierto, ¿viste el logo nuevo de Mateo? Me lo mostró en su estudio y quedó muy bien.

traduccion.en: By the way, did you see Mateo's new logo? He showed it to me in his studio and it came out very well.

dialogo.texto: Sí, es un puente azul con el sol detrás. Me encanta cómo quedó, sencillo y fuerte.

traduccion.en: Yes, it's a blue bridge with the sun behind it. I love how it came out, simple and strong.

dialogo.texto: A lo que íbamos: ¿qué necesitan para el segundo grupo? Puedo revisar el presupuesto gratis, cuando quieran, porque quiero que a Puente le vaya bien.

traduccion.en: Back to what we were saying: what do you need for the second group? I can check the budget for free whenever you want, because I want Puente to do well.

traduccion.en: Mateo and I need a clear proposal and one more guide. If you have time, on Friday I'll send you the list by email.

traduccion.en: Perfect, I'll be waiting for it. And I'll tell you about the congress as soon as I have the date.

dialogo.texto: Entonces quedamos así: tú mandas la lista, yo busco la fecha del congreso y Sofía nos pasa el horario del taller.

traduccion.en: So we agree like this: you send the list, I look for the date of the congress and Sofía gives us the schedule of the workshop.

objetivo.en: React spontaneously to news (surprise, disbelief, soft denial, resignation) with colloquial reactions.

traduccion.en: you don't say! no way! (surprise)

nota.en: Say “noh meh DEE-gahs”. It is a fixed phrase: digas is the negative command form, so it does not forbid anything. It can express real surprise or, with a flat tone, irony: you already knew.

traduccion.en: seriously? really?

nota.en: Say “ehn SEH-ryoh”. It asks the other person to confirm. A similar phrase is ¿de verdad?

traduccion.en: wow! how shocking!

nota.en: Say “keh FWEHR-teh”. It reacts to news that hits hard, good or bad. It is very frequent in Spain and is understood in Latin America.

traduccion.en: well, well! wow!

nota.en: Say “AHN-dah”. As an expression of surprise it is typical of Spain. In Latin America ¡anda! is mostly the command “go on!”, so as a surprise it sounds Spanish.

traduccion.en: no way! not at all!

nota.en: Say “keh BAH”: v sounds like b. It denies, softly or strongly, what the other person says or thinks: —¿Te aburriste? —¡Qué va!

traduccion.en: see? that's how it is!

nota.en: Say “yah BEHS”. You say it with resignation when something turns out the way it usually does. Do not confuse it with ya veo, which means “I see, I understand”.

traduccion.en: disbelief

nota.en: Say “een-kreh-doo-lee-DAHD”: the stress falls on the last syllable. It is the feeling of not believing what you hear.

traduccion.en: resignation

nota.en: Say “reh-seeg-nah-SYOHN”: the g is pronounced before the n, and the stress falls on the last syllable. It is accepting something you cannot change.

traduccion.en: the hotel owner or manager

nota.en: Say “oh-teh-LEH-roh”: the h is silent. The feminine form is la hotelera.

explicacion.en: Learners build the phrase with the present tense. «No me digas» uses the negative command form (digas), and it is a fixed phrase that means “You don't say!”, not a real order.
Ya veo means “I see, I understand”. To say “See? That's how it is!” with resignation, Spanish uses ya ves, with the other person as the subject.
“No way!” cannot be translated word by word. To deny something softly, Spanish says ¡qué va!

texto.en: Spoken Spanish is full of short reactions that you say before you think. This lesson has four families. Surprise: «¡No me digas!», «¡Qué fuerte!», «¡Anda!». Asking for confirmation: «¿En serio?», «¿De verdad?». Soft denial: «¡Qué va!», as in «¡Qué va! Me encantó». Resignation: «¡Ya ves!». They are fixed expressions: you do not conjugate or change them. «No me digas», for example, does not forbid anything; it simply means “you don't say”.

The same reaction can be happy or ironic, and only the tone (and the situation) tells you which. «¡No me digas!» after good news is sincere surprise; with a flat voice after something obvious («¡No me digas! ¿Otra vez tarde?») it means “I already knew”. In writing, the context has to do the work. «¡Qué va!» denies what the other person thinks or says, so it fits answers like «—¿Te aburriste? —¡Qué va!». «¡Anda!» and «¡Qué fuerte!» are very common in Spain; in Latin America you will understand them, but «¡No me digas!» and «¿En serio?» are safer.

contexto.en: Tuesday, January 23, 2035, about 6:30 p.m. After her day at Andes Vivos, Emma stops by the small office that she and Mateo have rented in La Floresta for Puente. Mateo is going through the email. Emma still works at Andes Vivos and prepares Puente in her free time. They use tú. Mateo has three pieces of news about Puente's first presale bookings.

dialogo.texto: Emma, qué bueno que llegaste. Tengo tres noticias del correo y quiero ver tu cara con cada una.

traduccion.en: Emma, I'm glad you made it. I have three pieces of news from the email and I want to see your face with each one.

dialogo.texto: Suena peligroso. Llevo todo el día en Andes Vivos y estoy cansada, pero la curiosidad es más fuerte que el cansancio. A ver, empieza.

traduccion.en: That sounds dangerous. I've been at Andes Vivos all day and I'm tired, but curiosity is stronger than tiredness. Let's see, go ahead.

dialogo.texto: La primera: un grupo de Canadá reservó seis personas para una de nuestras rutas. Ya mandaron el primer pago de la preventa.

traduccion.en: The first one: a group from Canada booked six people for one of our routes. They already sent the first payment of the presale.

dialogo.texto: ¡No me digas! ¿Seis personas? ¡Y todavía ni tenemos folleto!

traduccion.en: You don't say! Six people? And we don't even have a brochure yet!

dialogo.texto: Así como lo oyes. Se enteraron por una recomendación de Valentina.

traduccion.en: Just as you hear it. They found out through a recommendation from Valentina.

dialogo.texto: Valentina es un tesoro. Ayer me dijo que tenía amigos interesados, pero no pensé que iban a reservar tan rápido. ¿Y la segunda noticia?

traduccion.en: Valentina is a treasure. Yesterday she told me she had interested friends, but I didn't think they were going to book so fast. And the second piece of news?

dialogo.texto: La segunda es de un hotelero de Baños. Nos escribió que quiere regalar el desayuno a todos nuestros grupos de preventa.

traduccion.en: The second one is from a hotel owner in Baños. He wrote to us that he wants to give breakfast as a gift to all our presale groups.

dialogo.texto: ¿En serio? ¿A todos los grupos?

traduccion.en: Seriously? To all the groups?

dialogo.texto: En serio. Mira el correo, está firmado por él.

traduccion.en: Seriously. Look at the email, it's signed by him.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué bueno! Eso nos ahorra mucho dinero. ¿Y qué quiere a cambio?

traduccion.en: How great! That saves us a lot of money. And what does he want in return?

dialogo.texto: Que su hotel salga en el folleto. Me parece justo. Y según el correo, el desayuno incluye jugo, café y pan recién hecho.

traduccion.en: That his hotel appears in the brochure. It seems fair to me. And according to the email, the breakfast includes juice, coffee and freshly made bread.

dialogo.texto: A mí también. Eso lo podemos hacer sin problema. ¿Y la tercera noticia?

traduccion.en: To me too. We can do that with no problem. And the third piece of news?

dialogo.texto: La tercera no es tan buena. La primera factura se perdió. La mandé por correo y no aparece en ninguna parte.

traduccion.en: The third one is not so good. The first invoice got lost. I sent it by email and it doesn't show up anywhere.

dialogo.texto: ¡Ya ves! Apenas empezamos y ya se nos pierden los papeles.

traduccion.en: See? We've barely started and we're already losing our papers.

dialogo.texto: Tranquila, ya pedí otra copia y no habrá problema. Oye, por cierto, pensé que no querías este grupo. La semana pasada dijiste que era demasiado pronto.

traduccion.en: Relax, I already asked for another copy and there will be no problem. Listen, by the way, I thought you didn't want this group. Last week you said it was too soon.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué va! Dije que era pronto para el folleto, no para los clientes. Este grupo es justo lo que necesitamos.

traduccion.en: Not at all! I said it was too soon for the brochure, not for the clients. This group is exactly what we need.

dialogo.texto: Entonces me quedo más tranquilo. ¿Y sabes qué ruta quieren hacer?

traduccion.en: Then I feel calmer. And do you know which route they want to do?

dialogo.texto: No, dime tú.

traduccion.en: No, you tell me.

dialogo.texto: Quieren una ruta por la sierra con una noche en una comunidad y una visita al mercado.

traduccion.en: They want a route through the highlands with a night in a community and a visit to the market.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto, eso es justo lo que sabemos hacer. Solo me preocupa una cosa.

traduccion.en: Perfect, that's exactly what we know how to do. Only one thing worries me.

dialogo.texto: ¿Qué cosa?

traduccion.en: What is it?

dialogo.texto: Que lleguen los turistas de Canadá y todavía no tengamos todo listo.

traduccion.en: That the tourists from Canada arrive and we still don't have everything ready.

dialogo.texto: Para eso es la preventa: tenemos tiempo para preparar todo con calma.

traduccion.en: That's what the presale is for: we have time to prepare everything calmly.

dialogo.texto: Tienes razón. ¿Hay algo más?

traduccion.en: You're right. Is there anything else?

dialogo.texto: Y otra cosa pequeña: el hotelero preguntó si ya tenemos página web.

traduccion.en: And one more small thing: the hotel owner asked if we already have a website.

dialogo.texto: ¿Todavía no? ¡No me digas que se nos olvidó!

traduccion.en: Not yet? Don't tell me we forgot!

dialogo.texto: Qué va, la página está casi lista; solo falta el texto de las rutas.

traduccion.en: Not at all, the page is almost ready; only the text of the routes is missing.

dialogo.texto: Menos mal. El texto lo escribo yo este fin de semana. ¿Qué hacemos primero?

traduccion.en: Thank goodness. I'll write the text this weekend. What do we do first?

dialogo.texto: Yo pido la copia de la factura y tú le contestas al hotelero esta noche.

traduccion.en: I'll ask for the copy of the invoice and you answer the hotel owner tonight.

dialogo.texto: Trato hecho. Le escribo desde mi casa esta misma noche.

traduccion.en: Deal. I'll write to him from my home tonight.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Mañana revisamos el folleto con el desayuno incluido.

traduccion.en: Perfect. Tomorrow we'll go over the brochure with breakfast included.

dialogo.texto: Seis personas en preventa y un desayuno gratis. Para la primera semana, nada mal.

traduccion.en: Six people in presale and a free breakfast. For the first week, not bad at all.

dialogo.texto: Nada mal. Y una factura perdida, que ya es una buena anécdota.

traduccion.en: Not bad at all. And a lost invoice, which is already a good anecdote.

traduccion.en: See? That's how all agencies begin, with a lost invoice and plenty of enthusiasm.

objetivo.en: Recognize the regional colloquialisms for «great» (chévere, bacán, padre) and choose a neutral form depending on who you talk to.

traduccion.en: great, cool (Ecuador and other Andean countries)

nota.en: Say “CHEH-beh-reh”: the written accent marks the stress on CHEH, the v sounds like a b and the single r is quick, like the tt in “butter”. It has one form for masculine and feminine: un plan chévere, una playa chévere.

traduccion.en: great, cool (Ecuador, Peru, Chile)

nota.en: Say “bah-KAHN”: the stress falls on the last syllable, as the accent shows. It also has one form for masculine and feminine: un lugar bacán, una película bacán.

traduccion.en: great, cool (Mexico)

nota.en: Say “PAH-dreh”: the d is soft, like the th in “this”. As an adjective it means “great” in Mexico and has one form: una idea muy padre. El padre is still “the father”, so Mexicans enjoy the pun.

traduccion.en: great, brilliant

nota.en: Say “heh-NYAHL”: the g is a strong h and the stress falls on the last syllable. It is understood in every Spanish-speaking country.

traduccion.en: wonderful, terrific

nota.en: Say “ehs-too-PEHN-doh”: the stress falls on PEHN. The feminine form is estupenda. It sounds neutral and warm.

traduccion.en: excellent

nota.en: Say “ehk-seh-LEHN-teh”: the x sounds like “ks” and the c before e sounds like an s. It has one form for masculine and feminine. It is a little more formal.

traduccion.en: the regional word or expression

nota.en: Say “reh-hyoh-nah-LEES-moh”: the g before i is a strong h, and the stress falls on LEES. A regionalismo is a word that belongs to one region or country.

traduccion.en: the wink, the friendly nod

nota.en: Say “GEE-nyoh”: gu before i gives a hard g and the u is silent; the ñ sounds like “ny” in “canyon”. A regional word between friends is a guiño: a small sign that you belong.

explicacion.en: Many learners change the ending to -a for a feminine noun. Chévere has only one form for masculine and feminine, just like genial, padre or bacán: una playa chévere.
English says “What a cool plan!” with a. In Spanish exclamations, qué goes directly before the noun, with no article: ¡Qué plan chévere! or ¡Qué plan tan chévere!
English “cool” (great) is not frío: frío means cold in temperature or a cold person. To say “cool, great”, use chévere, bacán, padre or, for everyone, genial.

texto.en: In Spanish, “great” changes from country to country. In Ecuador and other Andean countries people say «chévere»; in Ecuador, Peru and Chile, «bacán»; in Mexico, «padre». All of them mean «genial» and they are invariable in gender: «un plan chévere», «una playa chévere», «una idea muy padre». You use them like any adjective, with «muy» («Está muy padre») or in an exclamation («¡Qué plan tan chévere!», «¡Qué chévere está tu departamento!»).

titulo.en: Choosing a word for your audience

texto.en: A regional word is a «guiño» between friends: it tells the other person where you are from. But if you write for a mixed audience, such as a brochure for tourists from many countries, choose a neutral word: «genial», «estupendo» or «excelente». These work everywhere. With someone from another country you can use their word as a game, but do not mix countries inside one sentence: «¡Qué padre!» in Quito sounds Mexican, and «¡Qué bacán!» in Guadalajara sounds like a visitor from Chile, Peru or Ecuador. Also remember that «padre» still means “father”: «mi padre» is my father, not a great person.

contexto.en: Sunday, January 21, 2035, in the middle of the morning. On a beach in Atacames, on the last day of their working weekend, Emma and Mateo are preparing the brochure for Puente. Mateo is from Guadalajara and Emma has lived in Ecuador for years. They use tú with each other and with a tourist from Chile who comes by and asks about a restaurant. Emma still works at Andes Vivos and prepares Puente in her free time.

dialogo.texto: Mateo, mira lo que escribí para el folleto: «Un paseo chévere por el centro de Atacames». Lo escribí esta mañana temprano, antes del desayuno.

traduccion.en: Mateo, look at what I wrote for the brochure: “A great walk through the center of Atacames”. I wrote it early this morning, before breakfast.

dialogo.texto: Se nota que llevas años en Ecuador. Yo escribiría «un paseo muy padre», que es como lo diría un mexicano.

traduccion.en: You can tell you've lived in Ecuador for years. I would write “a really great walk”, with padre, which is how a Mexican would say it.

dialogo.texto: ¿Muy padre? Dicho así parece que hablas de tu papá.

traduccion.en: Really padre? Said like that, it sounds like you're talking about your dad.

dialogo.texto: Es verdad, suena raro. En México «padre» también quiere decir «genial». Yo digo «qué padre está la playa» todos los días.

traduccion.en: True, it sounds odd. In Mexico “padre” also means “great”. I say “how great the beach is” every day.

dialogo.texto: Y en Ecuador decimos «chévere». ¡Qué chévere está la playa!

traduccion.en: And in Ecuador we say “chévere”. How great the beach is!

dialogo.texto: Los dos suenan perfecto, pero ¿para quién escribimos el folleto? Vienen turistas de Estados Unidos y de otros países.

traduccion.en: Both sound perfect, but who are we writing the brochure for? Tourists come from the United States and from other countries.

dialogo.texto: Es verdad. Si escribo «chévere», un turista de otro país puede no entender.

traduccion.en: True. If I write “chévere”, a tourist from another country may not understand.

dialogo.texto: Perdón, ¿ustedes saben dónde se come bien por aquí? Llegué ayer y todavía no encuentro un buen restaurante.

traduccion.en: Excuse me, do you know where one eats well around here? I arrived yesterday and I still haven't found a good restaurant.

dialogo.texto: Claro. Si te gustan los camarones, hay un restaurante a dos cuadras de aquí, frente al mar.

traduccion.en: Sure. If you like shrimp, there is a restaurant two blocks from here, facing the sea.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué bacán! Justo lo que quería. ¿Y es caro?

traduccion.en: How great! Just what I wanted. And is it expensive?

dialogo.texto: No, los precios están bien para un restaurante frente al mar. Con un jugo frío y unos camarones, el día queda completo.

traduccion.en: No, the prices are fine for a restaurant facing the sea. With a cold juice and some shrimp, the day is complete.

dialogo.texto: Bacán, esa palabra también la conozco. ¿De dónde eres?

traduccion.en: Bacán, I know that word too. Where are you from?

dialogo.texto: De Chile. Allá decimos «bacán» para todo: una película, un concierto, un amigo.

traduccion.en: From Chile. There we say “bacán” for everything: a movie, a concert, a friend.

dialogo.texto: Entonces los tres decimos lo mismo con palabras distintas: padre, chévere y bacán.

traduccion.en: So the three of us say the same thing with different words: padre, chévere and bacán.

dialogo.texto: Los entendí a los dos, aunque «padre» me sonó raro al principio.

traduccion.en: I understood both of you, although “padre” sounded odd to me at first.

dialogo.texto: Eso nos pasa con el folleto: vienen turistas de muchos países y no todos entienden todo.

traduccion.en: That's what happens to us with the brochure: tourists come from many countries and not everyone understands everything.

dialogo.texto: ¿Un folleto? ¿Trabajan en turismo?

traduccion.en: A brochure? Do you work in tourism?

dialogo.texto: Estamos preparando una agencia pequeña con Mateo. Se llama Puente.

traduccion.en: We are preparing a small agency together with Mateo. It's called Puente.

dialogo.texto: Puente, qué buen nombre. Entonces usen una palabra que entiendan todos.

traduccion.en: Puente, what a good name. Then use a word that everybody understands.

dialogo.texto: Eso pensamos nosotros. Para un público de varios países, «genial», «estupendo» o «excelente».

traduccion.en: That's what we thought. For an audience from several countries, “genial”, “estupendo” or “excelente”.

dialogo.texto: Las palabras de cada país son un guiño entre amigos, pero en el folleto va una palabra que sirve para todos.

traduccion.en: The words of each country are a wink between friends, but in the brochure goes a word that works for everyone.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y si yo quiero hablar como la gente de aquí? ¿Digo «chévere»?

traduccion.en: And if I want to talk like the people here? Do I say “chévere”?

dialogo.texto: Claro, aquí todos entienden «chévere». Pero si hablas con un mexicano, di «padre» y le vas a gustar.

traduccion.en: Sure, everybody here understands “chévere”. But if you talk to a Mexican, say “padre” and he will like you.

dialogo.texto: Es verdad, a mí me encanta cuando alguien lo dice.

traduccion.en: That's true, I love it when someone says it.

dialogo.texto: Entonces lo voy a usar mañana. Un guiño, me gusta. Bueno, voy a buscar ese restaurante. Gracias por todo.

traduccion.en: Then I'm going to use it tomorrow. A wink, I like that. Well, I'm going to look for that restaurant. Thanks for everything.

dialogo.texto: De nada. Que te vaya muy bien con los camarones y que te guste el restaurante.

traduccion.en: You're welcome. I hope it goes very well with the shrimp and that you like the restaurant.

dialogo.texto: Entonces el folleto dirá «un paseo genial por Atacames». ¿Te parece?

traduccion.en: So the brochure will say “a great walk through Atacames”. Does that sound good to you?

dialogo.texto: Me parece. Dejamos el regionalismo para hablar con amigos y ponemos «genial» en el papel.

traduccion.en: It does. We leave the regional word for talking with friends and put “genial” on paper.

dialogo.texto: Y para las redes ponemos una foto de la playa con la sombrilla y la frase «un fin de semana genial».

traduccion.en: And for social media we'll post a photo of the beach with the umbrella and the phrase “a great weekend”.

dialogo.texto: Buena idea. La frase la escribo yo y la foto la tomas tú.

traduccion.en: Good idea. I'll write the phrase and you take the photo.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Termino este párrafo y vamos por un jugo. Hoy el sol está fuerte.

traduccion.en: Perfect. I'll finish this paragraph and we'll go get a juice. The sun is strong today.

dialogo.texto: Trato hecho. Y esta tarde, el atardecer, que aquí es muy bonito.

traduccion.en: Deal. And this afternoon, the sunset, which is very beautiful here.

titulo.en: Es que… si yo te contara…

objetivo.en: Leave a sentence unfinished with «es que…» and «si yo te contara…» to excuse yourself, hesitate or hint there is a lot to tell.

traduccion.en: it's just that…, the thing is…

nota.en: Say “eh-SKEH”: es and que run together. It starts an excuse or an explanation, often with the voice hanging and a pause (written …): Es que… no he tenido tiempo. It is not a literal “it is that”.

traduccion.en: if I told you…

nota.en: Say “see yoh teh kohn-TAH-rah”: contara is the imperfect subjunctive of contar. The second half of the sentence is left out on purpose: it suggests that there is much more and that it is hard to believe.

traduccion.en: the excuse

nota.en: Say “ehks-KOO-sah”: the x sounds like “ks” and the stress falls on KOO. It is a reason you give to justify something. It is not used to say “excuse me”: for that, Spanish says disculpa or perdón.

traduccion.en: the pending task, the thing still to do

nota.en: Say “pehn-DYEHN-teh”. In Mexico and in Ecuador, un pendiente is something you still have to do: Tengo tres pendientes. In writing it is often used in the plural: la lista de pendientes.

traduccion.en: let's see

nota.en: Say “ah BEHR”: the v sounds like a b. It is a filler to start, to think or to ask for an explanation: A ver, empieza.

traduccion.en: you know (what I mean)

nota.en: Say “yah SAH-behs”. It appeals to what the other person already knows, so you do not have to say more: Ya sabes cómo son los trámites.

traduccion.en: the hint, the insinuation

nota.en: Say “een-see-nwah-SYOHN”: the stress falls on the last syllable. It is something you suggest without saying it clearly.

traduccion.en: to leave half-done, to leave unfinished

nota.en: Say “deh-HAHR ah MEH-dyahs”: the j is a strong h. You can leave a task or a sentence a medias, that is, half finished.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Es justo que no he tenido tiempo.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Es que… no he tenido tiempo.

explicacion.en: English “it's just that…” makes learners think of justo. But justo means “fair” or “exactly”. To start an excuse, Spanish uses es que, and it is followed by the reason in the indicative.

After si in this kind of sentence Spanish uses the imperfect subjunctive (contara), not the conditional (contaría). The conditional goes in the part that is left out: «Si yo te contara, no lo creerías».
Excusa is a noun (an excuse, a pretext). English “excuse me” is translated as disculpa, perdón or con permiso, not excusa.

texto.en: In conversation, Spanish speakers often start a sentence and leave it hanging. «Es que…» begins an excuse or an explanation and the voice stays up for a moment: «—¿Por qué no contestaste? —Es que… se me acabó la batería». It can also introduce something difficult: «Es que… no sé cómo decirte esto». «Si yo te contara…» goes further: it never ends, and the listener understands that there is much more to tell and that it is hard to believe. In writing, the three dots (…) show this suspended tone.

«Es que» is followed by the reason in the indicative («Es que… no he tenido tiempo»). «Si yo te contara…» is a conditional sentence with the second part left out: «si» + imperfect subjunctive («contara»), and the listener supplies the rest («…no lo creerías»). It is a way to hint without saying: an «insinuación». You can also leave something «a medias» with «ya sabes…» («you know…»). Use them with friends: with a boss or in a formal text, a complete reason sounds better than a hanging «es que…».

contexto.en: Friday, January 26, 2035, around eight in the evening. Mateo, in his studio, and Emma, at home in Guápulo after her day at Andes Vivos, go over Puente's pending tasks by video call. They use tú. Mateo asks why Emma has not sent a proposal to a client and why a guide's permit is delayed; he then asks about the last group Emma guided at Andes Vivos.

dialogo.texto: ¡Hola, Emma! ¿Me ves bien? ¿Me escuchas?

traduccion.en: Hi, Emma! Can you see me well? Can you hear me?

dialogo.texto: Te veo y te escucho perfecto, con tu lista de pendientes y todo. Se nota que ya te sientes jefe de oficina. ¿Empezamos?

traduccion.en: I see you and hear you perfectly, with your list of pending tasks and everything. You can tell you already feel like the office boss. Shall we start?

dialogo.texto: Desde el estudio se ve todo más tranquilo. Aquí no hay ruido, solo la lista y un café.

traduccion.en: From the studio everything looks calmer. There is no noise here, just the list and a coffee.

dialogo.texto: Qué suerte. Yo tengo a los vecinos con la música desde las seis.

traduccion.en: You are lucky. I have the neighbors with their music since six.

dialogo.texto: A ver, el primer pendiente: la propuesta para el segundo grupo. Te la pedí el miércoles y todavía no llega. ¿Qué pasó?

traduccion.en: Let's see, the first pending task: the proposal for the second group. I asked you for it on Wednesday and it still hasn't arrived. What happened?

dialogo.texto: Es que… esta semana tuve que traducir un documento urgente para Andes Vivos, y no me quedó tiempo.

traduccion.en: It's just that… this week I had to translate an urgent document for Andes Vivos, and I had no time left.

dialogo.texto: Entiendo, pero el cliente quiere la propuesta cuanto antes. ¿Me la mandas mañana?

traduccion.en: I understand, but the client wants the proposal as soon as possible. Can you send it to me tomorrow?

dialogo.texto: Sí, mañana mismo te la mando, lo prometo. Es una buena propuesta, solo falta revisar las fechas.

traduccion.en: Yes, I'll send it to you tomorrow, I promise. It's a good proposal, we only need to check the dates.

dialogo.texto: Gracias. Con eso me quedo tranquilo. Además, ya llegó la copia de la factura y el hotelero de Baños confirmó el desayuno.

traduccion.en: Thanks. That makes me feel calm. Besides, the copy of the invoice has already arrived and the hotel owner in Baños confirmed the breakfast.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué buena noticia! Entonces el grupo de Canadá ya tiene hotel y desayuno. Solo falta el guía.

traduccion.en: What good news! So the group from Canada already has a hotel and breakfast. We only need the guide.

dialogo.texto: Segundo pendiente: el permiso del guía. Debía llegar esta semana y se retrasó. ¿Hablaste con la oficina?

traduccion.en: Second pending task: the guide's permit. It was supposed to arrive this week and it got delayed. Did you talk to the office?

dialogo.texto: Sí, hablé con ellos. Es que… ya sabes cómo son los trámites: dicen que falta un sello, y luego otro.

traduccion.en: Yes, I talked to them. It's just that… you know how paperwork is: they say a stamp is missing, and then another one.

dialogo.texto: Ya sé, ya sé. Es una buena excusa, pero sin permiso el guía no puede trabajar con el grupo de Canadá.

traduccion.en: I know, I know. It's a good excuse, but without a permit the guide can't work with the group from Canada.

dialogo.texto: Lo sé, y por eso voy a llamar en cuanto abran la oficina.

traduccion.en: I know, and that's why I'm going to call as soon as the office opens.

dialogo.texto: Si quieres, te acompaño a la oficina cuando vayas.

traduccion.en: If you want, I'll go with you to the office when you go.

dialogo.texto: Gracias, pero prefiero ir sola; así no te quito tiempo.

traduccion.en: Thanks, but I prefer to go alone; that way I don't take up your time.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Último pendiente: ¿cómo te fue con el último grupo de Andes Vivos? Nos sirve para aprender.

traduccion.en: Perfect. Last pending task: how did it go with the last group at Andes Vivos? It helps us learn.

dialogo.texto: Ay, Mateo, si yo te contara…

traduccion.en: Oh, Mateo, if I told you…

dialogo.texto: …no lo creerías. Seguro que hubo niebla, el bus llegó tarde y alguien se quedó sin botas, ¿no?

traduccion.en: …you wouldn't believe it. I bet there was fog, the bus arrived late and somebody was left without boots, right?

dialogo.texto: Casi. Hubo niebla, el bus llegó tarde y un turista dejó la mochila en el restaurante. Y eso fue solo la mañana.

traduccion.en: Almost. There was fog, the bus arrived late and a tourist left his backpack in the restaurant. And that was only the morning.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y la mochila apareció? ¿O el turista tuvo que volver sin ella?

traduccion.en: And did the backpack turn up? Or did the tourist have to go back without it?

dialogo.texto: Sí, gracias a la mesera, que la guardó detrás del mostrador. Si yo te contara cómo la buscó él, con la cara roja…

traduccion.en: Yes, thanks to the waitress, who kept it behind the counter. If I told you how he looked for it, with his face red…

dialogo.texto: Ya me imagino la escena. Eres muy buena para dejar las historias a medias. Cada vez que dices «si yo te contara…» me quedo con ganas de más.

traduccion.en: I can already picture the scene. You are very good at leaving stories unfinished. Every time you say “if I told you…” I want more.

dialogo.texto: Es una insinuación, ya sabes. Una buena historia necesita un poco de misterio.

traduccion.en: It's a hint, you know. A good story needs a little mystery.

dialogo.texto: Pues yo quiero el final. ¿Me lo cuentas con un café?

traduccion.en: Well, I want the ending. Will you tell me over a coffee?

dialogo.texto: Trato hecho. Te la cuento entera, sin dejar nada a medias.

traduccion.en: Deal. I'll tell you the whole thing, without leaving anything half told.

dialogo.texto: Entonces anoto: propuesta mañana, permiso cuando abran la oficina y la historia completa con un café.

traduccion.en: Then I'll write down: proposal tomorrow, permit when the office opens and the full story over a coffee.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Y a ver, ¿hay algo más en la lista?

traduccion.en: Perfect. And let's see, is there anything else on the list?

dialogo.texto: Nada más por hoy. Pues nada, a descansar, que mañana hay mucho por hacer.

traduccion.en: Nothing else for today. Well, time to rest, because tomorrow there is a lot to do.

dialogo.texto: Pues nada, hasta mañana.

traduccion.en: Well, until tomorrow.
